responseMessageContents.text:
I'm setting up the full iOS app structure with Swift files for models, services, view models, views, and theming. The API uses passwordless login via email to get access tokens, and there's an AI conversation endpoint that accepts messages with optional conversation IDs.

I'm also mapping out the worker API endpoints for job management—creating jobs with goals and template modes, checking job status and progress, and retrieving job history. The template modes include BUG_FIX (confirmed), NEW_MODULE, and NEW_APP, though I'll allow flexible selection since the backend validates the values.

For the UI design, I'm going with a dark theme using near-black backgrounds and gold accents, organizing the interface into tabs for Chat, Builder, Status, and a login gate. On the concurrency side, I'm keeping the service on the main actor by default and marking DTOs as nonisolated, with JSON decoding happening on the background but within async functions that run on the main actor—acceptable for small payloads.

Now I'm setting up the file structure for the iOS project... ginView.swift, MainTabView.swift, ChatView.swift, WorkerView.swift, NewJobSheet.swift, and HealthView.swift to complete the view layer, then updating the app entry points. I'm keeping one type per file but grouping smaller data transfer objects together where it makes sense.

For the health response, the `routes` field might come through as an array of strings, so I'll decode it leniently and just extract the count. I'm using custom structs with optional fields to handle the uncertainty in the API response format.

For session persistence, I'll store the owner email in UserDefaults and keep the token in memory since it expires in 15 minutes anyway—Keychain would be more secure but this keeps things simple. Before each authorized request, I'll check if the token is near expiry and re-login with the stored email if needed. Since I'm unsure about the `expiresAt` format, I'll just track a local timestamp of the current time plus 12 minutes.

Writing all the files now...I'm writing out the complete app now, including the models, API service, view models, and all screens.
